name: wall-window
does: A window on the wall behind the head: a seam draws, the window opens out of it (title strip up, picture down) and plays a clip (by default this very video from 0:00), the title types, a progress line runs along the seam, a true tag types onto the picture, then it folds back into the seam before the cut. The head breaks the window's edge.
use_when: 'here's the full version', 'I filmed the whole process', any mention of a video or a recording the viewer can get; a clip that should feel like it hangs in the room
inputs: a CUT_WINDOWS entry over the window (behind the head)
the label and a true tag (TAG: this video's real length, or what the clip is)
the clip (SRC: clean.mp4, or a file dropped in the instance folder as fx/<id>/<file>.mp4) and where it starts (MEDIA_START)
WIN measured on a still of the shot: bare wall beside the head, the head breaking the window's near edge

notes.TAG: true facts only: the length is timeline.json total as m:ss
notes.WIN: x, y, w in px; the picture is 9:16 inside the frame; strip is the title bar's height
notes.T: all beats (seconds after A or spoken words); the clip starts on T.open (bound into fx.html by preset.py), so rerun preset.py when you move it
notes.SRC: a project-relative path the composition can load: clean.mp4, or fx/{{ID}}/clip.mp4 for a file in the instance folder

sfx.name: typing
sfx.what: the label types (placed by its start)
